mechanism: Nearshoring and friendshoring can increase demand for locally compliant flat steel; Ternium's Pesquería downstream lines and DRI-EAF shop can convert that demand into Mexican shipments, utilization, revenue, margins, and ADS-holder earnings, subject to commissioning, customer qualification, trade rules, steel pricing, cash conversion, and non-Mexican exposures.
catalyst: Downstream lines achieve disclosed utilization and customer qualification, the DRI-EAF shop commissions on the revised early-2027 schedule without material cost escalation, USMCA review outcomes preserve workable regional rules, Mexican shipments and margins rise, and operating cash flow covers remaining capex while attributable earnings improve.
invalidation: USMCA or tariff changes fragment regional supply chains; customers do not qualify or use Pesquería output; startup slips again; infrastructure constraints impede utilization; imports or weak demand depress steel pricing; or working capital, capex, Usiminas commitments, currencies, minority interests, and non-Mexican operations absorb the regional benefit.
